description: Pointsman is a decision service on Cloudflare Workers. A client system sends a state (a resident's road report, a new issue, a deploy's stack events) to `POST /v1/decide/{profile}`; a language model answers the profile's typed questions; the profile's rules turn the answers into an action (`auto`, `review` or a custom one); every decision is logged with its profile version and model. One Worker per integrator, deployed from a private config repository that holds the profiles. Clients: the FIWARE bridge, two GitHub Actions and MCP agents. The state author is the untrusted surface; token holders are trusted for their profiles; the operator is trusted.

trust_boundaries.boundary: `engine-api`: a finding matters if it is reachable from a request that carries a valid token, or from the `state`, `ref` or `callback_url` such a request carries, or from a model backend's response. trust_boundaries.boundary: **Engine → downstream**: the decision, the decision record and the signed callback are the engine's outputs; the client, the bridge, the Actions and the broker act on them (§1.8).

trust_boundaries.boundary: `config-repo`: reachable from a pull request to the config repository or from the operator's own command line; both are trusted authors (§1.7).
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from a pull request to the config repository or from the operator's command line; both are trusted authors

known_misuse.pattern: acting on a test: true decision as if it were logged
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Acting on a `test: true` decision as if it were logged (`R-IGNORE-TEST-DECISIONS`).
known_misuse.instead: check the test field; keep test tokens out of production clients

known_misuse.pattern: reading p as the model's accuracy and setting thresholds without a margin
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Reading `p` as "the model is 90 % accurate" and setting thresholds without a margin (`D-MODEL-ACCURACY`).
known_misuse.instead: treat p as the model's probability; keep a margin; re-check examples after model updates

known_misuse.pattern: citing the decision log as proof that a report was true or that a named person resolved it
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Citing the decision log as proof that a report was true or that a named person resolved it (`D-LOG-TRUTH`, `D-REVIEWER-IDENTITY`).
known_misuse.instead: treat the log as the engine's record; authenticate people in the client

known_misuse.pattern: one --profiles '*' token shared by every client
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Using one `--profiles '*'` token for every client, so the log cannot tell clients apart and a leak exposes every profile (`R-SCOPED-TOKENS`).

known_misuse.pattern: building deploy-watch's run or stacks from issue or pull-request text
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Building deploy-watch's `run` or `stacks` from issue or pull-request text (`R-ACTION-INPUTS`).
known_misuse.instead: set them in the workflow only

known_misuse.pattern: a callback receiver that acts without checking the signature and timestamp, or that is not idempotent
known_misuse.why_unsafe: A callback receiver that acts on the payload without checking the signature and timestamp, or that is not idempotent (`R-VERIFY-CALLBACK`).
known_misuse.instead: verify the HMAC and timestamp; dedupe on decision_id

known_misuse.pattern: a subscription that limits notification.attributes to the inputs so the result attribute never arrives and every notification decides again
known_misuse.why_unsafe: A bridge subscription that limits `notification.attributes` to the inputs, so the result attribute never arrives and every notification decides again (`R-BRIDGE-SUBSCRIPTION`).
known_misuse.instead: leave notification.attributes unset or include the result attribute

known_misuse.pattern: mcp.visible: true on a profile whose questions or decisions are not for every organization member
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Setting `mcp.visible: true` on a profile whose questions or decisions are not for every organization member (`R-MCP-VISIBLE`).

known_misuse.pattern: putting secrets or identifying free text into ref
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Putting secrets or an identifying free text into `ref` (`R-STATE-IS-DATA`).
known_misuse.instead: use an opaque reference such as an issue URL

known_misuse.pattern: sending personal data in state with the AI Gateway's logs on and no retention decision
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Sending personal data in `state` with the AI Gateway's logs on and no retention decision (`R-DATA-MINIMISATION`).
known_misuse.instead: set collect_logs: false or decide retention first

known_misuse.pattern: making a consequential action the policy's default so a missing fact or a steered answer falls through to it
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Making a consequential action (`publish`, `cancel`) the policy's default action, so a missing fact or a steered answer falls through to it (`R-REVIEW-PATH`).

open_questions.claim: Q1: Roles and the untrusted surface. We believe the untrusted surface is the `state` a client forwards (written by a state author who holds no token), plus everything a token holder can send within its scope; the operator, the Cloudflare account holder and reviewers with a valid token or grant are trusted; co-tenants, side channels and the model's training data are out of this layer.

Q2: Deployment shape. We believe the only supported deployment is one Worker per integrator, deployed from a private config repository; a shared hosted Pointsman serving several integrators is unsupported until it is designed.

Q3: Component carve and the bridge. We believe the bridge, the two Actions and the config-repo template belong in this one model as families; `examples/`, `site/`, `brand/`, `docs/spikes/`, `test/`, the build and check scripts, and the demo repository are out of scope; the bridge does not need a sibling model yet.
open_questions.proposed: yes; revisit the sibling question when a city runs the bridge in its own account.

open_questions.claim: Q4: Configuration support. We believe `MODEL_MODE=mock`, `PROFILE_SOURCE=bundled`, `FACTS_MODE=mock` and a plain-http model server are dev-only; `FACTS_MODE=off`, no `AI_GATEWAY_ID`, no `CALLBACK_SECRET` and no GitHub login are supported production postures; a deployment that drops `global_fetch_strictly_public` is unsupported.

Q5: Host side effects. We believe the engine fetches only the hosts listed in §1.5 (model backend, GSI, Valhalla, `callback_url`, GitHub, and the OAuth client-ID metadata URL), spawns nothing, reads no environment beyond bindings, and writes only D1, `OAUTH_KV` and the tile cache; the hole is what `@modelcontextprotocol/server` and `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider` may fetch on their own. We also believe the module-level caches and the callback claim behave as §1.5 says, and that Hono routes every `/v1/*` request through the token middleware.
open_questions.proposed: yes, with the metadata-document fetch as the only library-originated outbound call.

open_questions.claim: Q6: Redirects in the bridge. We believe the bridge follows redirects from the broker and from Pointsman (default `fetch` mode), unlike the engine's outbound calls; since both URLs are operator-set this is a trusted-collaborator edge and not a defect.
open_questions.proposed: yes, record it; make it a `VALID-HARDENING` candidate rather than a model claim.

open_questions.claim: Q7: Prompt injection. We believe steering the model's answers through the state is accepted by design: the model's answer is advisory, the typed answer set (`P-ANSWER-SHAPE`), the policy (`P-ACTION-FROM-POLICY`) and the `review` path contain it, and a report that only shows "I made the model answer X" is `BY-DESIGN: property-disclaimed`; a state that makes the engine return an answer outside the profile's set, or an action the policy does not produce for the answers, is `VALID`.

Q8: State size. We believe the engine sets no size or depth limit on `state`, and that the project chooses to disclaim this (the platform's body limit, the model backend's limits and edge rate limiting bound it) rather than promise a bound.
open_questions.proposed: disclaim (`D-STATE-SIZE`), with `R-RATE-LIMIT` as the integrator's obligation; alternatively name a limit and it becomes a §1.11 resource property.

open_questions.claim: Q9: `callback_url`. We believe any public https URL is accepted by design, that redirects are not followed and the receiver's body is ignored, that the payload holds no secret, and that an allow-list is not planned; a report that the engine POSTs a signed decision to a public URL the token holder chose is `BY-DESIGN`.

Q10: Fact lookup bounds. We believe the bounds in §1.7 (1000 positions, 200 samples, 16 and 9 tiles, 5 km, 3 s per fact, 10 s per tile load) are the intended guarantee, that exceeding them is `error` or `timeout`, and that this is a correctness-only property.

Q11: Fact data trust. We believe GSI tiles and the Valhalla server are trusted data sources, that an unknown legend colour fails closed, that the shelter list and route lengths are taken as published, and that the engine's own PNG and GeoJSON readers are the only parsers of that data.

Q12: Model backend trust. We believe the model backend is trusted to receive the state and its answers are untrusted data checked for shape; the HTTP adapter stores the configured model name and ignores the server's; Workers AI's reported model name is trusted; a backend that answers a well-formed wrong answer is `D-MODEL-ACCURACY`, not a vulnerability.

Q13: Test tokens at the boundary. We believe a `test: true` decision that a client acts on is the client's fault (`OUT-OF-MODEL: trusted-input` against `R-IGNORE-TEST-DECISIONS`), and that a test token reading or resolving a logged decision, reaching MCP, or receiving a callback would be `VALID` against `P-TEST-TOKEN-ISOLATED`.

Q14: Reviewer identity. We believe `by` and `resolved_by` are deliberately client-asserted, that the engine authenticates clients and only MCP people as persons, and that a client that lets an unauthenticated person resolve under any name is misusing the API, not finding a bug.

Q15: What the decision log proves. We believe the log proves what the engine received (by hash), which profile version and model answered, which rule fired and when, and for whom (client name); it does not prove the state was true, who wrote it, that the client acted, or that nobody with account access changed it; tamper evidence is disclaimed at correctness-only because the only actor who could tamper is out of scope.
Q16: `state_hash`. We believe `state_hash` is meant to show repeats and is not a pseudonymisation: a plain SHA-256 of canonical JSON lets anyone who can guess the state confirm it.
open_questions.proposed: yes, document it as a false friend.

open_questions.claim: Q17: Token lifetime and rate limits. We believe tokens have no expiry and the engine has no per-token rate limit or quota, that both are disclaimed for now with edge and gateway limits as the operator's job, and that expiry is a `VALID-HARDENING` candidate rather than a model gap.
open_questions.proposed: disclaim both; keep expiry on the hardening list.

open_questions.claim: Q18: Scope off-switches. We believe the only two ways to act beyond a single profile scope are a `--profiles '*'` token and an OAuth person (every MCP-visible profile), and that `mcp.visible` is the only per-profile control for people.

Q19: OAuth client handling. We believe open dynamic client registration and client-ID metadata documents are intended, that the consent page and GitHub membership are the controls, and that PKCE, state binding, consent handles and encrypted grant props are relied on as the OAuth library's contract (`OUT-OF-MODEL: dependency-contract` when the library breaks them).

Q20: Bridge adversary. We believe whoever can write entities, Decision entities or completed Task entities in the broker tenant is the bridge's in-scope adversary, the broker itself is a trusted collaborator, queue messages are the bridge's own, and the broker's access control owns who may trigger decisions and resolve reviews.

Q21: Bridge outputs. We believe everything the bridge writes to the broker comes from the profile's closed answer set and fixed metadata, except the Task `name` (an entity attribute's text), fact `source` strings, and `reviewedBy`/`finalAction` passed through from the resolving app, and that consumers must treat those as data.

Q22: The Actions. We believe `run`, `stacks` and `labels` are trusted workflow-author inputs, that issue text and stack event text are attacker-influenced prompt text, and that a steered `cancel` of a healthy deploy is a correctness issue (`D-MODEL-ACCURACY`, `P-WATCH-FAILSAFE`), not a security one.

Q23: Version binding and venue. We believe the model should be bound to commit `e1d3591` until the first release tag, revised on the §1.16 triggers, and that a `SECURITY.md` should be added that names the private reporting channel and links this document.
open_questions.proposed: yes; create `SECURITY.md` in the same pull request that ratifies wave 1.

open_questions.claim: Q24: Triage policy. We believe `strict` is right while the draft is unratified; after wave 1 and 2 are answered, `relaxed` would let the remaining assumptions close low-blast-radius reports provisionally.
